title: Documentary Photography
description: The unflinching photograph — the FSA archive and the pioneers of the form.

items.title: Migrant Mother
items.description_narrative: This iconic photograph captures Florence Owens Thompson and her children in a pea-pickers' camp during the Great Depression, embodying the widespread struggles of the era. Lange's powerful composition emphasizes the family's resilience and the profound human impact of economic hardship.
items.tags: poverty, migration, family, mother, documentary photography, social realism, hardship, iconic

items.title: Toward Los Angeles
items.description_narrative: Dorothea Lange's "Toward Los Angeles" captures a poignant scene of individuals navigating the American landscape during a period of economic hardship. The image reflects the transient nature of life and the search for new opportunities in a changing nation.
items.tags: migration, documentary photography, great depression, black and white, journey, social realism, hardship
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID fsa.8b31801.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Tractored Out, Childress County Texas
items.cultural_context: American documentary photography, Great Depression era
items.description_narrative: This photograph captures the stark reality of agricultural displacement during the Great Depression, showing a family's meager possessions against the backdrop of their land. It powerfully illustrates the impact of mechanization and economic hardship on rural American communities in the late 1930s.
items.tags: documentary photography, Great Depression, Dust Bowl, rural America, economic hardship, social realism, displacement
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID ppmsc.00232.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: The Steerage
items.description_narrative: Alfred Stieglitz's 'The Steerage' captures European immigrants in the lowest deck of a transatlantic ship, a pivotal work in photographic history. It is celebrated for its modernist composition, emphasizing the interplay of lines, shapes, and textures over purely documentary narrative.
items.tags: photography, modernism, immigration, social commentary, early 20th century, New York, composition
items.credit_line: DwGsXk0l3l7fkw at Google Cultural Institute, zoom level maximum

items.title: Floyd Burroughs, cotton sharecropper
items.description_narrative: This striking portrait captures Floyd Burroughs, a cotton sharecropper, through the lens of renowned photographer Walker Evans. Evans's direct photographic style frequently documented the lives of individuals impacted by the Great Depression.
items.tags: great depression, documentary photography, sharecropper, portrait, black and white, american, 1930s

items.title: Allie Mae Burroughs
items.cultural_context: American, Great Depression era, Documentary Photography
items.description_narrative: Walker Evans's iconic portrait captures Allie Mae Burroughs, a sharecropper's wife, with an unwavering gaze, taken in Hale County, Alabama. Made in 1936, this stark black and white image became a central part of Evans's influential documentary work on the American South during the Great Depression.
items.tags: portrait, documentary photography, great depression, rural life, social realism, american south, black and white, 1930s
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID fsa.8c52248.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: American Gothic, Washington, D.C.
items.description_narrative: Gordon Parks's iconic photograph, "American Gothic, Washington, D.C.," features Ella Watson, a charwoman, standing stoically with a broom and mop before an American flag. This powerful image, often seen as a reinterpretation of Grant Wood's painting, critiques racial and economic disparities in 1940s America.
items.tags: portrait, documentary, social realism, american, civil rights, poverty, photography
items.credit_line: This image is available from the United States Library of Congress's Prints and Photographs division under the digital ID fsa.8b14845.This tag does not indicate the copyright status of the attached work. A normal copyright tag is still required. See Commons:Licensing.

items.title: Power house mechanic working on steam pump
items.cultural_context: Social documentary photography, Early 20th Century American
items.description_narrative: This powerful photograph captures a lone mechanic, immersed in the intricate work of maintaining a large steam pump. Lewis Hine's lens elevates the labor of the industrial worker, emphasizing the skill and dedication essential to modern progress.
items.tags: labor, industry, worker, machinery, documentary photography, early 20th century, social realism

items.title: Breaker Boys, Pennsylvania
items.description_narrative: Lewis Hine's "Breaker Boys, Pennsylvania" powerfully captures young laborers amidst the harsh realities of early 20th-century coal mining. This impactful image was a crucial part of Hine's extensive documentation efforts, which played a significant role in advocating for child labor reform in the United States.
items.tags: child labor, coal mining, documentary photography, social reform, industrial, progressive era, early 20th century, poignant

items.title: Spinner in a Cotton Mill
items.description_narrative: This powerful photograph by Lewis Hine captures a young spinner at work in a cotton mill, exposing the widespread issue of child labor in early 20th-century America. Hine's documentary approach aimed to raise public awareness and advocate for social reform.
items.tags: child labor, documentary photography, social reform, industrialization, early 20th century, American, mill worker

items.title: Bandit's Roost
items.description_narrative: This striking photograph captures a dense, narrow alley in a New York City tenement district, revealing the harsh realities of urban poverty at the turn of the 20th century. Jacob Riis created this image as part of his groundbreaking work to expose squalid living conditions and advocate for social reform.
items.tags: urban poverty, tenement life, New York City, social documentary, photojournalism, muckraking, late 19th century

items.title: Ancient Ruins in the Canyon de Chelly
items.description_narrative: Timothy H. O'Sullivan's photograph captures ancient ruins nestled within the dramatic landscape of Canyon de Chelly. This image serves as an important visual record of archaeological sites in the American Southwest during the 19th century.
items.tags: ruins, canyon, american west, landscape, photography, historical, archaeological, exploration

items.title: Yosemite Valley from Inspiration Point
items.description_narrative: Carleton Watkins's 'Yosemite Valley from Inspiration Point' captures a panoramic vista of the iconic valley. This renowned work presents the breathtaking natural grandeur of one of America's most celebrated landscapes.
items.tags: yosemite, landscape, nature, scenic, grand, vista
items.credit_line: 6wHjXKTSmvR6Hg at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Boulevard du Temple
items.description_narrative: This pioneering daguerreotype captures a Parisian street scene, notably including one of the first human figures ever photographed, a shoe shiner and his customer. Its exceptionally long exposure time of several minutes meant moving traffic and pedestrians vanished, leaving the bustling boulevard deceptively empty except for the stationary figures.
items.tags: early photography, daguerreotype, parisian street, urban landscape, 19th century, historical, pioneer
items.credit_line: Scanned from The Photography Book, Phaidon Press, London, 1997.

items.title: The Open Door
items.medium: Salted paper print from a calotype negative
items.description_narrative: William Henry Fox Talbot's 'The Open Door' captures a simple rural doorway, illuminating a broom and a lantern with natural light. This pioneering calotype exemplifies early photographic exploration of everyday subjects and the interplay of light and shadow.
items.tags: early photography, calotype, still life, doorway, rustic, light and shadow, 19th century

items.title: View from the Window at Le Gras
items.description_narrative: This landmark image, captured by Nicéphore Niépce, is widely recognized as the world's first successful permanent photograph created with a camera obscura. The heliograph depicts the view from a window at Niépce's estate in Saint-Loup-de-Varennes, France.
items.tags: photography, landscape, heliography, early photography, camera obscura, French, invention

items.title: Geronimo
items.description_narrative: Edward S. Curtis, a renowned American photographer, captured this powerful portrait of Geronimo, the prominent Apache leader. This work is part of Curtis's extensive project to document the disappearing cultures of Native American peoples, showcasing individual dignity and strength.
items.tags: photography, portrait, geronimo, apache, native american, historical, ethnographic, documentation
